stem: Two lines are graphed in the \(xy\)-plane, and the labeled points lie on the lines. If the two lines are the graphs of the equations in a system, what is the \(x\)-coordinate of the solution to the system?
solution: The line through \((0, -3)\) and \((3, 3)\) has slope \(2\): \(y = 2x - 3\).
The line through \((0, 9)\) and \((9, 0)\) has slope \(-1\): \(y = -x + 9\).
Set them equal: \(2x - 3 = -x + 9\), so \(3x = 12\) and \(x = 4\). (The intersection is \((4, 5)\).)
verify:
x = symbols('x')
P = [(q['x'], q['y']) for q in figure['points']]
line = lambda a, b: (b[1] - a[1])*(x - a[0])/(b[0] - a[0]) + a[1]
l1, l2 = line(P[0], P[1]), line(P[2], P[3])
assert {sympify(c['expr']) for c in figure['curves']} == {l1, l2}
xs = solve(Eq(l1, l2), x)
assert xs == [4]
assert [Rational(s) for s in spr_answers] == xs
